title: Topological phase transition in a symmetric blockade structure
authors: Johannes Mögerle, Simon Fell, Tobias F. Maier, Ali Otaifi, Lode Pollet, Nicolai Lang, Hans Peter Büchler
abstract: We present a numerical study of a blockade Hamiltonian with a local $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry. For such models, the existence of a topologically ordered ground state has been proven rigorously for weak Rabi driving [T. F. Maier et al., PRX Quantum 6, 030340 (2025)]. However, the phase diagram beyond weak driving is still an open question. We perform large-scale infinite-size density matrix renormalization group (iDMRG) simulations on a cylinder and map out the full phase diagram of the model. We find a single continuous phase transition between the topologically ordered phase and a trivial paramagnetic phase, and confirm numerically the stability of the topologically ordered phase up to Rabi drives comparable to the characteristic energy scale of the system. Furthermore, we compute the excitation gaps and show that the charge gap remains open across the phase transition and charges become confined in the trivial phase. On the other hand, the gap in the symmetric sector closes at the transition, consistent with the condensation of flux excitations.
summary: This paper investigates the topological phase transition in a blockade Hamiltonian on a honeycomb lattice, which models systems like Rydberg arrays. Using iDMRG simulations, the authors map the full phase diagram, revealing a continuous transition between a topologically ordered state and a trivial phase. The findings confirm the robustness of the topological order across a wide range of driving parameters.
main_problem: The study aims to map out the full phase diagram of a blockade Hamiltonian possessing a local Z2 symmetry, particularly in regimes beyond weak Rabi driving.
main_result: The authors found a single continuous phase transition separating a topologically ordered phase from a trivial paramagnetic phase, confirming the stability of the topological order up to significant Rabi drives.
method: The research employs large-scale infinite-size density matrix renormalization group (iDMRG) simulations on a cylinder geometry, supplemented by perturbation theory for gap calculations.
model_or_system: The system is a blockade Hamiltonian defined on a honeycomb lattice, involving four two-level systems per site. The Hamiltonian includes terms for Rabi coupling (H_Omega), detuning (H_Delta), and both intra-site (H_V) and inter-site blockade interactions (H_U).
key_observables: Charge gap (remains open across the transition), excitation gap in the symmetric sector (closes at the transition), and Wilson loop expectation values.
important_parameters: Rabi drive strength (Omega), detuning (Delta), and blockade interaction strengths (U, V). The analysis explores various limits, such as weak ($\Omega \ll \Delta$) and strong ($\Omega \gg \Delta$) coupling.
main_assumptions: The analysis often assumes the limit of infinite on-site blockade ($V 	o \infty$) to simplify the Hilbert space to single excitations per site.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the honeycomb lattice setup and the local Z2 symmetry operator. Figure 2 details the iDMRG setup on a cylinder, defining flux and loop operators.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the model and its symmetries, then analyzes the system in perturbative limits (weak and strong coupling) to calculate excitation and charge gaps. Finally, it presents the full phase diagram mapping using iDMRG simulations.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the stability and phase boundaries of topological order in engineered quantum simulators, which is highly relevant for understanding strongly correlated quantum materials and quantum computation architectures.
